es.summary: Acumulación excesiva de grasa en hepatocitos sin consumo significativo de alcohol, asociada a resistencia a la insulina y síndrome metabólico.
key_points: La EHGNA se clasifica en hígado graso simple y esteatohepatitis (MASH).
La pérdida de peso del 7‑10 % mejora la esteatosis y la inflamación.
ALT y AST suelen estar elevadas, con razón ALT/AST >1.
Complicaciones incluyen fibrosis, cirrosis y carcinoma hepatocelular.
Control de comorbilidades (diabetes, dislipidemia) es esencial.

pathophysiology: Resistencia a la insulina aumenta la lipólisis y libera ácidos grasos libres al hígado.
Exceso de ácidos grasos se esterifica formando triglicéridos hepáticos.
Estrés oxidativo y citocinas provocan inflamación (MASH).
Fibroblastos hepáticos activados generan colágeno → fibrosis.
risk_factors: Dieta alta en fructosa y grasas saturadas.
signs_symptoms: Dolor o sensación de plenitud en hipocondrio derecho.
Ascitis y edema en enfermedad avanzada.
diagnostics: ALT y AST elevadas; ALT > AST y razón <1.
GGT y fosfatasa alcalina pueden estar aumentadas.
Ecografía abdominal muestra ecogenicidad hepática aumentada.
Elastografía o FibroScan evalúa grado de fibrosis.
Biopsia hepática para confirmar MASH y grado de inflamación.
treatment: Pérdida de peso 7‑10 % mediante dieta hipocalórica y ejercicio.
Dieta mediterránea, limitar azúcares simples y grasas saturadas.
Control estricto de glucemia y lípidos (metformina, estatinas).
Vitamina E (antioxidante) y pioglitazona en casos seleccionados.
complications: Hipertensión portal con ascitis y varices esofágicas.
Enfermedad hepática terminal y necesidad de trasplante.
nursing_care: Monitorear peso diario y signos de ascitis/edema.
Evaluar enzimas hepáticas y perfil metabólico cada 3‑6 meses.
Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos; restringir sodio <2 g/día.
Promover actividad física gradual según tolerancia.
Educar sobre dieta, abstinencia de alcohol y adherencia a medicamentos.
patient_teaching: Seguir dieta baja en grasas saturadas, azúcares y sodio.
Realizar ejercicio aeróbico al menos 30 min, 5 veces/semana.
Evitar consumo de alcohol y tabaco.
Controlar glucemia y lípidos; asistir a controles médicos.
Reconocer signos de complicaciones: ictericia, dolor abdominal intenso, edema.

evidenced_by: fatiga al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
outcomes: Nivel de actividad: el paciente realiza actividades de la vida diaria sin fatiga excesiva en 2 semanas.
Resistencia: el paciente aumenta su tiempo de caminata continua a 20 min en 4 semanas.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y tolerancia al ejercicio al ingreso y cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar cambios y planificar actividades apropiadas.

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso cada 30 min durante actividades prolongadas.
interventions.rationale: Previene la fatiga excesiva y mejora la adherencia al plan de ejercicio.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de pacing y establecimiento de metas realistas.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la autogestión y evita el sobreesfuerzo.

interventions.action: Registrar y monitorear la frecuencia cardíaca y saturación de O₂ antes y después del ejercicio.
interventions.rationale: Detecta intolerancia temprana y posibles complicaciones.

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapia para iniciar programa de ejercicio aeróbico progresivo.
interventions.rationale: Promueve mejora de la capacidad funcional de forma segura.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico: el paciente mantiene ingesta y salida de líquidos dentro de ±500 mL/día en 3 días.
Edema/ascitis: ausencia de aumento de edema periférico o ascitis en 1 semana.

interventions.action: Monitorear peso diario y registrar cambios de ≥0,5 kg.
interventions.rationale: Detecta retención de líquidos temprana.

interventions.action: Evaluar presencia de edema, distensión abdominal y fluctuación de la pared abdominal.
interventions.rationale: Identifica signos de acumulación de líquidos.

interventions.action: Restringir ingesta de sodio a <2 g/día y registrar consumo de alimentos.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la retención de agua y mejora el control de ascitis.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Permite cálculo preciso del balance hídrico.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de sobrecarga de líquidos (aumento de peso rápido, edema).
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz y la búsqueda de atención.

interventions.action: Colaborar con el médico para ajustar diuréticos según necesidad.
interventions.rationale: Optimiza el manejo farmacológico del exceso de líquidos.

en.summary: Excessive accumulation of fat in hepatocytes without significant alcohol consumption, associated with insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome.
key_points: NAFLD is classified into simple steatosis and steatohepatitis (NASH).
A weight loss of 7‑10 % improves steatosis and inflammation.
ALT and AST are usually elevated, with ALT/AST ratio >1.
Complications include fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
Control of comorbidities (diabetes, dyslipidemia) is essential.

pathophysiology: Insulin resistance increases lipolysis and releases free fatty acids to the liver.
Excess fatty acids are esterified forming hepatic triglycerides.
Oxidative stress and cytokines provoke inflammation (NASH).
Activated hepatic fibroblasts produce collagen → fibrosis.
signs_symptoms: Pain or fullness sensation in the right hypochondrium.
Ascites and edema in advanced disease.
diagnostics: Elevated ALT and AST; ALT > AST and ratio >1.
GGT and alkaline phosphatase may be increased.
Abdominal ultrasound shows increased hepatic echogenicity.
Elastography or FibroScan assesses fibrosis stage.
Liver biopsy confirms NASH and inflammation grade.
treatment: Weight loss 7‑10 % via hypocaloric diet and exercise.
Mediterranean diet, limit simple sugars and saturated fats.
Strict control of glucose and lipids (metformin, statins).
Vitamin E (antioxidant) and pioglitazone in selected cases.
complications: Portal hypertension with ascites and esophageal varices.
End‑stage liver disease and need for transplant.
nursing_care: Monitor daily weight and signs of ascites/edema.
Assess liver enzymes and metabolic profile every 3‑6 months.
Record fluid intake and output; restrict sodium <2 g/day.
Promote gradual physical activity per tolerance.
Educate on diet, alcohol abstinence, and medication adherence.
patient_teaching: Follow a low‑saturated‑fat, low‑sugar, low‑sodium diet.
Engage in aerobic exercise at least 30 min, 5 times/week.
Monitor glucose and lipids; attend medical appointments.
Recognize signs of complications: jaundice, severe abdominal pain, edema.

evidenced_by: fatigue during activities of daily living
outcomes: Activity level: the patient performs activities of daily living without excessive fatigue in 2 weeks.
Endurance: the patient increases continuous walking time to 20 min in 4 weeks.

interventions.action: Assess energy level and exercise tolerance at admission and each shift.
interventions.rationale: Allows identification of changes and planning of appropriate activities.

interventions.action: Plan rest periods every 30 min during prolonged activities.
interventions.rationale: Prevents excessive fatigue and improves adherence to the exercise plan.

interventions.action: Teach the patient pacing techniques and realistic goal setting.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates self‑management and avoids overexertion.

interventions.action: Record and monitor heart rate and O₂ saturation before and after exercise.
interventions.rationale: Detects early intolerance and potential complications.

interventions.action: Coordinate with physiotherapy to initiate a progressive aerobic exercise program.
interventions.rationale: Promotes safe improvement in functional capacity.

outcomes: Fluid balance: the patient maintains intake and output within ±500 mL/day in 3 days.
Edema/ascites: no increase in peripheral edema or ascites in 1 week.

interventions.action: Monitor daily weight and record changes ≥0.5 kg.
interventions.rationale: Detects early fluid retention.

interventions.action: Assess for edema, abdominal distension, and abdominal wall fluctuation.
interventions.rationale: Identifies signs of fluid accumulation.

interventions.action: Restrict sodium intake to <2 g/day and record food consumption.
interventions.rationale: Reduces water retention and improves ascites control.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output each shift.
interventions.rationale: Allows precise calculation of fluid balance.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on signs of fluid overload (rapid weight gain, edema).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and seeking care.

interventions.action: Collaborate with the physician to adjust diuretics as needed.
interventions.rationale: Optimizes pharmacologic management of excess fluid.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Signs of acute liver failure may include hypotension, altered mental status, fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, ascites, jaundice, or fluid overload (Shah et al., 2023).

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Signs and symptoms of cirrhosis include ascites dark-colored urine decreased urine output digestive problems edema hepatic encephalopathy jaundice light-colored stools motor dysfunction pruritus shortness of breath unexplained weight loss

sections.complications.0.quote: This scarring sometimes leads to cirrhosis or liver cancer .

sections.complications.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: The Model of End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) Score is used to predict survival of patients with cirrhosis and is a tool used to prioritize organ allocation for liver transplantation.

sections.complications.3.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.complications.4.quote: Signs and symptoms of cirrhosis include ascites dark-colored urine decreased urine output digestive problems edema hepatic encephalopathy jaundice light-colored stools motor dysfunction pruritus shortness of breath unexplained weight loss

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: These include administering medications documenting daily weights and abdominal girth measurement educating patients monitoring laboratory values, such as sodium levels monitoring vital signs and intake and output
